scope: Opt-in `#module "a.b";` logical owners, order-independent #load membership, schema-1 nominal declaration tuples (module, kind, name) and an opt-in `coax deps --declarations` report (coax.declarations.v1) of unit owners, declaration IDs and resolved references from the checked graph. Identity only: lookup stays flat, C spellings and generated code are unchanged.

policy.checks: 27 checks, 27 passed (11 new for module IDs, claims, membership order independence and tuple encoding)
policy.seed: coax/bootstrap/sources.c and sources.h refreshed with coax/refresh-sources-seed.sh; the bootstrap regenerates them byte for byte

native_transport.owners: Computed after the load traversal in reverse finishing order (topological): a claim owns itself, an unclaimed unit folds SU_owner_join over its loaders' owners, so the result never depends on load or traversal order.

errors.E0606: two canonical units claim one module ID
errors.E0607: an unclaimed unit reached under two owners

native_transport.masking: The directive bytes are blanked in the composed input like #load, so line numbers and generated code are unchanged.

covers: owner and members share one module; legacy identities are null; references carry target IDs
relocation into another directory and reordering loads/declarations preserve every ID
moving a declaration between members of one owner preserves its ID
module, kind and name changes change IDs
independent same-spelling equal-layout declarations have distinct IDs; one graph still has one flat namespace
two canonical units claiming one ID fail (E0606) at the second claim
an unclaimed member under two owners fails (E0607) at the second load; its own claim resolves it
a canonical diamond and an unowned extra loader keep one owner
invalid, nested, repeated or truncated claims fail (E0605); comments and strings never claim
member diagnostics and #authority checks stay with the member unit
a claim changes no generated C or line numbers; deps schema 1 is unchanged

regressions.bootstrap: coax/build.sh bootstrapped the snapshot and verified provenance; the sources seed regenerated identically

legacy_corpus.baseline_compiler: coax0 0.25.0, checked build 9f1f223c514a from the release cache
legacy_corpus.corpus: coax/tests/pass/*.coax, coax/examples/*.coax, coax/book/examples/*.coax, verse/hud.coax, verse/everglade/guard-types.coax, each as program and --library
legacy_corpus.result: 236 non-empty `coax c` outputs from 120 files are byte-identical between the 0.25.0 baseline and this compiler before the version bump; 4 inputs fail identically in both

limits: No qualified imports, private/public boundaries, reexports, content revisions, target manifests, cache keys or persistent engine/protocol identity (separate r1a children).
The checker inlines untyped literal constants (CK_copy_expr), so their uses are not reported as references; typed constants are.
Declarations in units without an owner report a null ID rather than a derived one.
Generated (#import_proto) declarations take the owner of their importing unit and are marked generated.

golden_gate.attribution: Not caused by this change: the shots differ from goldens in authored page content (sandbox and haunted-house now draw a GALAXY button their goldens lack; home pages differ in live relay content). The compiler change emits byte-identical C for the legacy corpus. No goldens were approved; they belong to the pages' authors.
